1: After Moses' death God tells Joshua to lead the people across the Jordan and promises, "I will be with you." Joshua is to meditate on the law day and night. The people pledge to obey him.
Courage comes from God's presence, not from Joshua's own strength.
2: Two spies enter Jericho and are hidden by Rahab, a prostitute, who confesses that Israel's God is God of heaven and earth. She is promised safety and hangs a scarlet cord from her window.
A pagan woman with a bad past is saved by faith. She appears in the family tree of Jesus.
3: The priests carry the ark into the flooded river. The water stops, and all Israel crosses on dry ground.
God repeats for a new generation what he did at the Red Sea.
4: One man from each tribe carries a stone from the riverbed to build a memorial at Gilgal.
"When your children ask, What do these stones mean?" Faith is passed on by telling the story.
5: The men born in the desert are circumcised. Israel keeps Passover, eats the produce of the land, and the manna stops. Joshua meets the commander of the Lord's army.
The desert years are over. Joshua learns that the battle is God's.
6: Israel marches around Jericho for seven days with the ark and trumpets. At the shout the walls collapse. Rahab and her family are spared.
The city falls to obedience and worship, not to siege engines.
7: Israel is beaten at the small town of Ai. The cause is found: Achan secretly kept plunder devoted to God. He confesses and is punished.
One person's hidden sin harms the whole community.
8: This time Israel takes Ai by an ambush. Joshua builds an altar on Mount Ebal and reads the whole law aloud to everyone, including women, children and foreigners.
Victory is followed by renewing the covenant.
9: The people of Gibeon pretend to come from far away, wearing worn-out clothes, and win a treaty. Israel did not ask the Lord. The oath is kept, and they become servants.
Decisions made without prayer bring trouble. A promise still has to be kept.
10: Five kings attack Gibeon. Joshua marches all night to help, God sends hailstones, and the day is lengthened at Joshua's prayer. The south is conquered.
11: A coalition of northern kings is defeated at the waters of Merom, and Hazor is burned.
Joshua left nothing undone of all that the Lord commanded Moses.
12: A list of the kings conquered east and west of the Jordan, thirty-one in Canaan.
13: Joshua is old and much remains unconquered. The land east of the Jordan is described. The tribe of Levi receives no territory.
The Lord himself is Levi's inheritance.
14: At eighty-five Caleb asks for the hill country he scouted forty-five years earlier, giants and all, and receives Hebron.
Caleb "wholly followed the Lord", and his faith has not aged.
15: The borders and towns of the tribe of Judah. Caleb gives his daughter springs of water.
Judah, the tribe of David and of Christ, receives its place.
16: The land given to Joseph's son Ephraim. They fail to drive out the Canaanites of Gezer.
Half-finished obedience will cause problems later.
17: The land of Manasseh, including the share of Zelophehad's daughters. The tribe complains that it needs more room, and Joshua tells them to clear the forest.
18: The tabernacle is set up at Shiloh. Seven tribes still have no land, so Joshua has it surveyed and casts lots. Benjamin receives its share.
"How long will you put off taking possession?"
19: Land is allotted to Simeon, Zebulun, Issachar, Asher, Naphtali and Dan. Joshua receives his own town last.
The leader takes his share after everyone else.
20: Six towns are named where a person who kills by accident can find safety.
Mercy and justice are built into the settlement of the land.
21: The Levites receive forty-eight towns spread among all the tribes.
"Not one of all the good promises the Lord had made failed; all came to pass."
22: The eastern tribes go home and build a large altar. The others prepare for war, thinking it is rebellion, until they learn it is a memorial of shared faith.
Ask before you assume the worst of your brothers.
23: Old Joshua reminds the leaders that God fought for them and warns them not to mix with the nations' gods.
"Not one word has failed." God's faithfulness calls for ours.
24: At Shechem Joshua retells Israel's history and calls for a decision. "As for me and my house, we will serve the Lord." The people renew the covenant. Joshua dies.
Faith is a choice each generation has to make.
